accepted.s: The Gandhara school of art developed mainly in which region?
o: The middle Ganga valley around Mathura
The north-western frontier around Peshawar, Taxila and the Swat Valley
accepted.x: The Gandhara school developed in the north-western frontier region, particularly around Peshawar, Taxila and the Swat Valley in present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
accepted.tq: Use the geographical cluster to identify the art school.
accepted.sec: Gandhara school - foreign influence, patron dynasty, region  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets of influences is associated with Gandhara art?
accepted.x: Gandhara art reflects Hellenistic Greek, Roman and Persian influences in combination with Indian artistic traditions.
accepted.tq: Test the complete influence-list rather than a single familiar influence.
accepted.sec: Gandhara school - foreign influence, patron dynasty, region  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gandhara art is generally dated to which period?
accepted.x: The Gandhara school flourished approximately from the 1st to the 5th century CE.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the period of Gandhara from the dates of the other schools.
accepted.sec: Gandhara school - foreign influence, patron dynasty, region  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which dynasty introduced and patronised the Gandhara school of art, particularly under the line of Kanishka?
accepted.x: The Gandhara school was introduced by the Kushanas and flourished under the line of Kanishka.
accepted.tq: Apply the patron-dynasty association without confusing it with the regional schools.
accepted.sec: Gandhara school - foreign influence, patron dynasty, region  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the dominant religious theme of Gandhara art?
o: Mahayana Buddhism represented through Buddha and Bodhisattvas
Jainism represented through Yaksha figures alone
Theravada Buddhism represented only through symbols
accepted.x: Gandhara art predominantly expressed Mahayana Buddhism and commonly depicted the Buddha with Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya.
accepted.tq: Separate the religious theme of Gandhara from the themes of Mathura and Amaravati.
accepted.sec: Gandhara school - foreign influence, patron dynasty, region  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya are associated with which subject in Gandhara sculpture?
accepted.x: Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya are Bodhisattvas frequently associated with the Mahayana Buddhist theme of Gandhara art.
accepted.tq: Identify the religious figures linked with the Gandhara theme.
accepted.sec: Gandhara school - foreign influence, patron dynasty, region  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhara used grey or blue-grey schist and later stucco.
2. Mathura used spotted red sandstone.
3. Amaravati used white limestone associated with Palnadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Grey schist and stucco are associated with Gandhara, spotted red sandstone with Mathura, and white Palnadu limestone with Amaravati.
accepted.tq: Match each school with its characteristic material before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which art school is most characteristically associated with spotted red sandstone?
accepted.x: Spotted red sandstone is the characteristic material of the Mathura school.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the three schools through their sculpture material.
accepted.sec: Material → school  [other exams]

accepted.s: White limestone, particularly Palnadu limestone, was the principal material of which school?
accepted.x: The Amaravati school is associated with white limestone, also described as Palnadu limestone or white marble.
accepted.tq: Use the material-to-school association as the deciding clue.
accepted.sec: Material → school  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: White Palnadu limestone is associated with Amaravati, not Gandhara. Gandhara chiefly used grey schist and later stucco.
accepted.tq: Find the single material-school reversal among otherwise correct pairs.
accepted.sec: Material → school  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Art school)
 a. Gandhara
 b. Mathura
 c. Amaravati
 d. Amaravati in its mature phase

List-II (Association)
 i. Satavahanas and later Ikshvakus
 ii. Kushanas
 iii. Ikshvakus and Mahayana themes
 iv. Kushanas, with continuation in the Gupta age

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Gandhara is linked with the Kushanas; Mathura with the Kushanas and later Gupta age; Amaravati with the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus; and its mature phase with the Ikshvakus and Mahayana themes.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure patron pair and eliminate codes containing a misplaced dynasty.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which school flourished in the Ganga valley and was patronised by the Kushanas, with continuity into the Gupta age?
accepted.x: The Mathura school developed in the Ganga valley, began under the Shungas, flourished under the Kushanas and continued in the Gupta age.
accepted.tq: Combine location, patronage and continuity to identify Mathura.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best represents the themes of the Mathura school?
o: Only Jataka stories in crowded narrative reliefs
Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical subjects, including Yakshas, Yakshis and royal portraits
Only scenes of city life and local dress
Only Mahayana Buddha images and Bodhisattvas
accepted.x: Mathura art included Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical subjects, along with Yaksha-Yakshi figures and royal portraits.
accepted.tq: Use the broad multi-religious theme to distinguish Mathura from the other schools.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Amaravati art is primarily associated with which combination?
o: Satavahanas and later Ikshvakus, white limestone and Buddhist narratives
Guptas, red sandstone and royal portraits
accepted.x: Amaravati was patronised by the Satavahanas and later the Ikshvakus; it used white limestone and depicted Jatakas, the life of the Buddha and narrative reliefs.
accepted.tq: Check patron, material and theme together rather than relying on one clue.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The three schools of Gandhara, Mathura and Amaravati flourished approximately side by side during which cultural phase?
accepted.x: Gandhara, Mathura and Amaravati flourished side by side during the Kushana-Satavahana age.
accepted.tq: Use the common contemporaneous period to separate these schools from later artistic traditions.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the geographical distribution of the three major schools?
o: Gandhara in the north-west, Mathura in the Ganga valley and Amaravati in Andhra
Gandhara in Andhra, Mathura in the north-west and Amaravati in the Ganga valley
All three were concentrated in the north-western frontier
Gandhara in the Ganga valley, Mathura in Andhra and Amaravati in the north-west
accepted.x: Gandhara was located in the north-west, Mathura in the Ganga valley and Amaravati in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Compare the regional locations in one fixed geographical sequence.
accepted.sec: Art school → patron dynasty, material, theme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the emergence of the anthropomorphic Buddha image is correct?
o: Only Amaravati produced the first anthropomorphic Buddha image.
The Buddha was never represented through symbols before the Gupta age.
The Buddha was represented in human form from the Mauryan period onward without interruption.
The Buddha was first shown in human form during the Kushana period, while the earliest school between Gandhara and Mathura remains debated.
accepted.x: The Kushana period marks the first major use of the Buddha in human form. Both Gandhara and Mathura produced such images in the 1st century CE, and priority between them is debated.
accepted.tq: Separate the certain period from the disputed priority between Gandhara and Mathura.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: Before the anthropomorphic Buddha image became established, which of the following was used to represent the Buddha?
o: Symbols such as a throne, footprints, wheel, tree and stupa
Scenes of Sati and city life
accepted.x: Before anthropomorphic representation, the Buddha was worshipped aniconically through symbols including the throne, footprints, wheel, tree and stupa.
accepted.tq: Recognise the symbolic or aniconic phase of Buddhist representation.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Hinayana and Mahayana worship in the context of Buddha representation?
o: Hinayana used symbolic worship, whereas Mahayana worshipped idols.
Hinayana worshipped idols, whereas Mahayana rejected all images.
Both schools exclusively used royal portraits.
Both schools rejected symbols and adopted only narrative reliefs.
accepted.x: Hinayana is associated here with symbolic worship, while Mahayana encouraged the worship of Buddha images or idols.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed meanings of two closely associated Buddhist traditions.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who introduced symbol worship known as Chaitika Vada in Andhra?
accepted.x: In Andhra, symbol worship or Chaitika Vada was introduced by Mahadeva.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the religious teacher from the later art historians associated with Amaravati.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Ayakapatas of Amaravati represent the Buddha primarily through:
o: Symbols rather than a human figure
accepted.x: Amaravati Ayakapatas show the Buddha through symbols, reflecting the aniconic tradition.
accepted.tq: Apply the aniconic-symbolic distinction to a specific Amaravati object.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: Standing Buddha images became prominent in which phase of the Mathura school?
accepted.x: Standing Buddha images became prominent in the Gupta phase of the Mathura school.
accepted.tq: Use the phase-specific development rather than the broader school association.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Manukwar seated Buddha is noted for Gupta tranquillity. The Sultanganj bronze Buddha is a Gupta work, while Ayakapatas represent the Buddha symbolically.
accepted.tq: Find the precisely matched object-feature pair among related Buddhist images.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Sultanganj bronze Buddha is notable for being more than:
accepted.x: The Sultanganj bronze Buddha is a Gupta-period image measuring over two metres in height.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct magnitude without confusing it with monumental stupa dimensions.
accepted.sec: Buddha image - first anthropomorphic depiction debate, earliest human images  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Dharmachakra mudra of the Buddha represents:
accepted.x: Dharmachakra mudra symbolises the turning of the wheel of law and is associated with the Buddha’s first sermon at Sarnath.
accepted.tq: Link each mudra to its distinctive event rather than its hand position alone.
accepted.sec: Mudras of the Buddha → event depicted  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which mudra is represented by the Buddha touching the earth with the right hand?
accepted.x: Bhumisparsha mudra shows the right hand touching the earth, symbolising enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and calling the earth to witness against Mara.
accepted.tq: Use the physical gesture to identify the mudra and its event.
accepted.sec: Mudras of the Buddha → event depicted  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Abhaya mudra, with the right palm raised, conveys:
accepted.x: The raised right palm in Abhaya mudra signifies fearlessness and protection; it is also associated with reassurance after enlightenment and the subduing of Nalagiri.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the raised palm from the lowered palm and lap gestures.
accepted.sec: Mudras of the Buddha → event depicted  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which mudra depicts the Buddha’s hands placed in the lap in meditation?
accepted.x: Dhyana mudra is represented by the hands resting in the lap and signifies meditation before or at enlightenment.
accepted.tq: Identify the mudra from the hand position.
accepted.sec: Mudras of the Buddha → event depicted  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Varada mudra is associated with:
accepted.x: Varada mudra is shown with a lowered open palm and signifies boon-giving or charity.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the lowered open palm from the raised Abhaya palm.
accepted.sec: Mudras of the Buddha → event depicted  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Gandhara and Mathura representations of the Buddha?
o: Gandhara figures are slender and emotional, whereas Mathura figures are crowded narrative scenes.
Gandhara figures have heavy toga-like robes and Mathura figures wear transparent clinging garments.
Gandhara figures generally have shaved heads, whereas Mathura figures have wavy hair and top-knots.
Both schools used identical drapery and physiognomy.
accepted.x: Gandhara sculpture is marked by heavy, toga-like robes with deep folds, while Mathura sculpture commonly shows a transparent, clinging garment.
accepted.tq: Compare the drapery of the two schools to avoid swapping their visual features.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mathura — muscular, robust and smiling figures
Amaravati — slender, dynamic and emotional figures
Gandhara — slender figures showing intense movement
accepted.x: Slender, dynamic and emotional figures are characteristic of Amaravati. Gandhara is known for realistic, Apollo-like faces and spiritual calm.
accepted.tq: Locate the swapped physiognomical feature among the three schools.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Which statement about the hair treatment in the three schools is correct?
o: Mathura and Gandhara used identical hair treatment in every image.
Amaravati is specifically defined by wavy hair and top-knots.
Gandhara commonly shows wavy hair and a top-knot, while Mathura shows a shaved head or snail-shell curls.
Gandhara shows only shaved heads, while Mathura shows flowing Persian hair.
accepted.x: Gandhara commonly depicts wavy hair with a top-knot, whereas Mathura depicts a shaved head or snail-shell curls.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive hair conventions to separate Gandhara from Mathura.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: A plain or little-ornamented halo is especially associated with which school?
accepted.x: Gandhara images generally have a plain or little-ornamented halo. Mathura is associated with the Jnanachakra halo, while Amaravati depicts the Buddha on a lotus in Padmasana.
accepted.tq: Match the halo treatment with the correct school rather than the figure’s posture.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Which art school is characterised by frontal, single icons of the Buddha?
accepted.x: Mathura is characterised by frontal, single icons, unlike Gandhara’s standing Buddha in Greek attire and Amaravati’s crowded narrative compositions.
accepted.tq: Identify the composition type associated with Mathura.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: The depiction of Yakshas and Gandharvas dancing around the Buddha is characteristic of:
accepted.x: Amaravati compositions are narrative, crowded and full of movement; Yakshas and Gandharvas are shown dancing around the Buddha.
accepted.tq: Infer the school from the presence of movement and surrounding narrative figures.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Amaravati art has been called a ‘living art’ mainly because it expresses:
accepted.x: Amaravati is called a living art because of its strong expression of human feelings and emotional movement.
accepted.tq: Connect the descriptive title with its stated artistic quality.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Which school is described as depicting all the important events of the Buddha’s life?
accepted.x: Amaravati is described as the only art school depicting all important events of the Buddha’s life.
accepted.tq: Use the exceptional claim to identify the correct school.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Percy Brown described Amaravati art as the pinnacle of Indian art and associated it with:
accepted.x: Percy Brown regarded Amaravati as the pinnacle of Indian art and described its quality as dynamic beauty, or Jeevakala.
accepted.tq: Recall the critic’s exact evaluative phrase and its associated school.
accepted.sec: Depiction features compared - drapery, hair, halo, physique, narrative

accepted.s: Amaravati is also known by which historical names in relation to its location?
accepted.x: The Amaravati centre is associated with Dharanikota and Dhanyakataka, on the bank of the Krishna in the old Guntur district.
accepted.tq: Use the historical-name pair to identify the Amaravati centre.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: Amaravati, the principal centre of the Amaravati school, was located on the bank of which river?
accepted.x: Amaravati was situated on the bank of the Krishna in the old Guntur district.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the river associated with Amaravati from other Andhra rivers.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: Which site became the main centre of the Amaravati school under the Ikshvakus?
accepted.x: Nagarjunakonda became the main centre of the Amaravati school under the Ikshvakus.
accepted.tq: Link the Ikshvaku phase with its principal artistic centre.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a noted centre or site of the Amaravati school in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Taxila is a major Gandhara site, not an Amaravati-school site in Andhra Pradesh. Goli, Ghantasala and Bhattiprolu are associated with Amaravati art.
accepted.tq: Separate the Andhra site-list from the north-western Gandhara region.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: Which site is associated with the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Bhattiprolu is associated with the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the site linked with the superlative claim.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: The mature or final phase of the Amaravati school developed mainly under which dynasty?
accepted.x: The mature or final phase of the Amaravati school occurred under the Ikshvakus and included Mahayana themes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the later mature patron from the earlier Satavahana patronage.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: The first depiction of Sati in Indian art is found in which context?
o: A Mathura royal portrait of the Gupta period
A Gandhara sculpture of the Kushana period
An Amaravati-school sculpture of the Ikshvaku period
accepted.x: The first depiction of Sati in Indian art is found in an Amaravati-school sculpture belonging to the Ikshvaku period.
accepted.tq: Combine the school, dynasty and distinctive subject in the correct association.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: The sculptors associated with the Amaravati school were known as:
accepted.x: The sculptors of the Amaravati school were called Selavardhakulu.
accepted.tq: Recall the specialised occupational term linked with Amaravati sculptors.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: Who publicised Amaravati art through the work titled ‘Tree and Serpent Worship’?
accepted.x: James Fergusson publicised Amaravati art through his work Tree and Serpent Worship and called it the ‘Epitome of Indian architecture’.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the art historian associated with the work from the critic who praised its beauty.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: James Fergusson referred to Amaravati art as the:
accepted.x: James Fergusson called Amaravati art the ‘Epitome of Indian architecture’.
accepted.tq: Match the exact evaluative title with its author and school.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: The influence of Amaravati art spread to which of the following regions?
o: Sri Lanka, South-East Asia and later Gupta art
Central Asia without influence on Gupta art
accepted.x: Amaravati art influenced Sri Lanka, particularly Anuradhapura, South-East Asia and later Gupta art.
accepted.tq: Select the complete geographical and chronological range of influence.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: Anuradhapura, in the context of Amaravati art, is located in:
accepted.x: Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka was one of the regions influenced by Amaravati art.
accepted.tq: Use the named site to identify the region reached by Amaravati influence.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP

accepted.s: The Purna-Kumbha motif of Amaravati art is used as:
o: The emblem of the Andhra Pradesh State Government
The official seal of Sri Lanka
The symbol of the Kushana dynasty
The emblem of the Union Public Service Commission
accepted.x: The Purna-Kumbha motif of Amaravati art forms the emblem of the Andhra Pradesh State Government.
accepted.tq: Connect an art motif with its present institutional use.
accepted.sec: Amaravati school sites in AP
